Alice.summary: Alice's view that truth is relative to a single subject of discourse does not contradict the Law of Excluded Middle.

Bob.summary: Accepting both Alice's view and the Law of Excluded Middle leads to a contradiction.

c1.text: Every proposition concerns only one subject of discourse, and is true or false only relative to that subject.

c2.text: A proposition is not true in relation to any subject of discourse other than its own.

c3.text: According to the Law of Excluded Middle, for a proposition p concerning subject S, if p is not S-true, then p is S-false.

c4.text: Alice's view that truth is relative to a single subject of discourse does not contradict the Law of Excluded Middle.

c5.text: Accepting both Alice's view and the Law of Excluded Middle leads to a contradiction.

c6.text: The proposition 'Murder is wrong' (r) is an ethical proposition.

c7.text: The proposition r is not mathematically true.

c8.text: The proposition 'r is not mathematically true' belongs to the subject of ethics.

c9.text: The proposition 'r is not mathematically true' is ethically true.

c10.text: The proposition 'r is not mathematically true' is not mathematically true.

c11.text: According to the Law of Excluded Middle, for any proposition p and subject S, if 'p is not S-true' is not S-true, then p is S-true.

c12.text: The proposition r is mathematically true.

a.note: Alice accepts and holds the Law of Excluded Middle restricted to the domain S (if not S-true, then S-false).

h1.text: In 'it is not true that "p is not true"', the first 'true' and the second 'true' cannot be about the same subject of discourse.

b.note: If the two truth predicates cannot share a subject, the double-negation step r5 (both mathematical) is undercut, weakening Bob's argument.

h2.text: The proposition 'r is not mathematically true' belongs to the subject of discourse of art rather than ethics.

h3.text: The proposition 'r is not mathematically true' is artistically true.

c.note: Assuming 'r is not mathematically true' belongs to art, it is artistically true (rc1) and thus not mathematically true (rc2), deriving c10 and reaching Bob's conclusion as before.
